definition: The shared resolver in src/lib/server/action-context.ts (userContext, orgContext, projectContext) that every server action and API route starts from: user, active organization, database, feature permission and demo read-only check in one place.
The return shape of every server action: { success: true, data? } or { success: false, error } (src/lib/action-result.ts). Actions return failures rather than throwing.
The project timeline of who did what (activity_events plus record-specific history tables). Outside email, approvals and status changes are logged here.
A reusable group of estimate lines (for example a wall type) that can be priced as one unit, exported to a phase estimate, or copied into another job.
Who a project surface is for: staff (the company's own users), owners (clients) or vendors (subcontractors and suppliers). Owners and vendors see only records shared with their audience.
src/lib/__tests__/architecture-baseline.json: the frozen list of existing violations of the architecture standard. Counts may only fall.
A saved copy of a schedule's dates (schedule_baselines) used to measure slippage.
The on-premises agent that reads from and writes to the desktop accounting system, talking to Compass through signed HTTPS requests. Compass never connects to the accounting database directly.
A priced change to an accepted contract (project_change_orders). Approval revises the contract budget.
A recognition board where staff send cards tied to company values. Its name and values are configurable per company in Settings. Code and tables use the {values} placeholder prefix in this manual.
A job-cost classification from the accounting system (sage_cost_codes, project_field_cost_codes), used on estimate lines, POs, time and budgets.
Cloudflare's serverless SQLite database. Compass's single relational store (binding DB).
A field report for one project and day: work done, crew, weather, photos, and items that can become to-dos.

A separate deployment (wrangler env demo) with its own database and no scheduled jobs or outside integrations, seeded with the neutral example company Summit Ridge Builders. There is also a read-only demo user and organization in the main deployment.
A configurable division of work (for example construction, design, home services, product sales), each with its own job-number prefix and workflow. Departments can be switched on or off per company.
A folder under src/lib/domain/<module>/ that owns a set of tables: store.ts (all writes), rules.ts (pure logic), access.ts (who may).
The TypeScript ORM used for the schema (src/db/schema*.ts) and queries.
A priced scope for a project (project_estimates and lines). Several estimates may exist per job; acceptance turns one into contract value.
A set of linked jobs across departments, for example a design job and the construction job it leads to (project_families, project_family_phases).

A named capability (for example project-photos) with read/create/update/delete actions, checked by canFeature in src/lib/permission-enforcement.ts. Role defaults can be overridden per role, team or user.
The industry-standard application-for-payment summary and continuation-sheet formats that pay applications follow.
The human-facing project number. Format and prefixes are configurable per company and department; numbers are reserved and never reused (project_number_reservations, project_number_retirements).
A project's position in its pipeline (lead, estimating, contracted, in progress, closed and so on). Labels are configurable per company (project_job_statuses).
The adapter that builds the Next.js app into a Cloudflare Worker (@opennextjs/cloudflare).
The client who commissions the work. Owners sign in to a limited, permission-scoped view of their own projects.
The background job that writes a Drive copy of each changed record (estimates, change orders, logs and so on) after a quiet period, so the project's Drive folder holds a durable record.
A progress-billing request in G702/G703 form. Approved for billing, it becomes visible to the owner and is matched to an accounting invoice number.
A grouping of estimate or schedule work (for example a design phase) that can be proposed, approved and billed separately.
The standard printable view of every document (estimate, change order, pay app, log), rendered from the same data the screen uses.
An optional module for selling catalog products: versioned catalogs and prices, customer orders, rentals, and public order pages. Code and tables use the {sales} placeholder prefix in this manual.
A commitment to a vendor or supplier for a scope or materials, created from an awarded bid or directly (project_operations of kind purchase order plus project_purchase_order_lines).
A CI check that freezes today's count of a violation and fails if it grows (or shrinks without the baseline being updated).
Request for information: a question to the design team or a vendor, tracked with replies (project_rfis).
Request for quote sent to vendors for a scope; replies become bids that can be compared and awarded.
An owner choice of finish or product (project_selection_decisions, project_finish_selections), with requests, decisions and links to procurement.
A Next.js function in src/app/actions/ marked "use server" that the browser calls directly. All mutations go through one.
A column or row that deliberately freezes a value as it was when a document was signed, sent or approved. Named *_snapshot or commented // snapshot:.
The only file allowed to insert, update or delete a domain's tables (one writer per table).
The neutral example company used in the demo deployment and in this manual's examples.
An assignable task on a project (project_operations of kind to-do), with events, reminders and links to daily logs. Finished items are ticked by people, never automatically.
Outside email sent through sendTrackedEmail with a reply address tied to the record, so replies are imported back to the same thread, notification and Activity.
A subcontractor or supplier. Vendors can be invited to projects and see only what is shared with the vendor audience (RFQs, POs, documents, schedule items).
A permission-scoped area of the app: a project's staff workspace, the owner portal, the vendor portal, internal (non-project) workspaces such as the office duty log.
The hosted identity provider used for sign-in, SSO and invitations (pluggable behind src/lib/auth.ts).
